# Feature: Guaranteed User-Input Masking (explicit markers + contextual detection)

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-008
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

Give the user a way to **guarantee** that a value they supply never reaches the LLM, while
keeping that value usable by tools.

Today `UserInputVault.redact()` is pure shape matching (email / SSN / card / phone / API key).
Shape matching cannot be a guarantee: Yantra is used across countries and regions, and there is
no universal shape for a username, a password, a national ID, or an account number. A user who
types `enter website xyz with username u1, password p1` currently sends `u1` and `p1` straight
to the model.

This feature adds three layers with explicitly different guarantee levels:

| Layer                           | Guarantee    | Mechanism                                          |
| ------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| **Explicit markers** — `@{...}` | **Absolute** | User-declared. No inference, no locale assumption. |
| **Keyword look-around**         | Best-effort  | `password p1` → tokenize `p1`. English-anchored.   |
| **Shape patterns**              | Best-effort  | Existing set, plus VIN (ISO-3779 check digit).     |

The explicit marker is the product promise. The heuristics are defense-in-depth for users who
did not mark anything, and the documentation must never present them as a guarantee.

## 2. Technical Context

### Approach

**1. Segment model instead of chained `String.replace()`.**

The central architectural change. Redaction currently runs a sequence of `.replace()` passes over
one flat string, so every pass can see — and corrupt — what the previous pass produced. That is
tolerable for today's long, distinctive shapes and unacceptable once a user can mark an arbitrary
2-character value.

The parser instead produces a **segment list**:

```ts
type InputSegment =
  | { readonly kind: 'literal'; readonly text: string }
  | { readonly kind: 'value'; readonly tag: UserInputValueTag; readonly value: string };
```

Every detector maps over **literal segments only**, splitting each into further literal/value
segments. A value segment is structurally unreachable — no later pattern can match into it,
partially consume it, or re-tokenize it. Rendering joins the list, emitting `{{user:tag:N}}` for
value segments. This makes "a marked value is never processed again" a property of the data
structure rather than of pass ordering.

**2. Marker grammar (`@{...}`).**

`@` was chosen over `$`, `#`, and `!` on delivery-survival grounds, which is the actual threat to
a CLI tool: `${...}` expands in both bash and PowerShell double-quoted arguments (the value is
destroyed _before_ Yantra sees it), `#` opens a YAML comment and goals are persisted into workflow
YAML, and `!` triggers bash history expansion. `@{` is inert in bash, PowerShell, cmd, and YAML.

```
@{value}                -> {{user:secret:N}}          bare form, generic tag
@password{value}        -> {{user:password:N}}        tagged form
@{a{b}c}                -> value is `a{b}c`           balanced braces consume naturally
@{p\}1}                 -> value is `p}1`             backslash escape
@{a\\b}                 -> value is `a\b`
@{C:\Users\ranjith}     -> value is `C:\Users\ranjith` non-escape backslash stays literal
@@                      -> literal `@`                the opt-out (`@@{x}` renders `@{x}`)
```

**3. Precedence.** Markers are parsed first and win outright. Keyword look-around runs next over
literal segments — before shape patterns, so `password 4111111111111111` is tagged `password`
rather than `credit_card`. Shape patterns run last.

**4. Ingress enforcement.** Parsing moves to the top of `runAgenticTask`, before the run directory
is created and before `locationHandoffFor` reads the goal. All three agentic CLI commands (`do`,
`ask`, `research`) route through `runAgenticTask`, so one chokepoint covers every surface and any
future caller. This also closes an existing leak: raw `request.goal` currently reaches
`promoteAgentTrace` at `orchestrator.ts:1119` as both `description` and `synthesisGoal`, which
**writes it into a saved workflow YAML file on disk**.

**5. Echo-masking is tiered separately from redaction.** `mask()` currently does a blind
`split/join` of each stored value across model-visible tool output. Correct for a 16-digit card,
catastrophic for `@{u1}` — every `u1` substring in every page result would be rewritten. Redaction
stays unconditional; masking becomes length-tiered and placeholder-aware.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

No overrides — see `.spec-lite/memory.md`.

Reinforced standing rules this feature leans on:

- _Security_: "Sanitize every model-visible payload." The vault is the user-value half of that;
  this feature makes it declarative rather than inferential.
- _Architecture_: "Keep sanitizer, secret resolution … outside prompt text." Marker parsing is a
  runtime concern; the model is told only what `{{user:...}}` means, never the marker syntax.
- _Testing_: "use property tests for sanitizer and protocol invariants" — TASK-002 and TASK-006
  carry property tests, not just examples.
- _CLI UX_: no new flags. The marker is inline syntax; the failure mode is a validation error.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

N/A — no persisted schema changes. Two in-memory run-scoped structures:

### Entities & Attributes

- **`InputSegment`** (discriminated union, transient):
  - `kind` (`'literal' | 'value'`) — discriminator
  - `text` (string) — literal branch only
  - `tag` (`UserInputValueTag`) — value branch only
  - `value` (string) — value branch only; the raw sensitive value, never rendered

- **`UserInputVault`** (existing, extended): `valueByPlaceholder`, `placeholderByValue`,
  `countersByTag` — unchanged shapes.

- **`UserInputValueTag`** (extended union). Existing: `email`, `phone`, `ssn`, `credit_card`,
  `api_key`, `auth_param`. Added: `secret`, `username`, `password`, `pin`, `otp`, `national_id`,
  `vin`, `account`, `dob`, `address`.

  Marker tag names are **identical** to internal tag names so no mapping table exists.
  `auth_param` is internal-only (derived from URL structure) and is rejected as a marker tag.
  `ssn` is retained for the existing US-shaped detector; keyword-detected national identifiers use
  `national_id`.

### Indexes & Constraints

- Marker tag set is **closed**. An unknown tag (`@passwrd{...}`) is a parse error, not a silent
  fallback to `secret` — a typo must fail loudly rather than quietly mislabel.
- Marked value length: 1–2048 characters. Empty or whitespace-only is a parse error.
- Input containing a literal `{{user:...}}` sequence is rejected at ingress — the placeholder
  namespace is reserved, and accepting user-typed placeholders would let `resolve()` substitute a
  value the user never intended.

## 5. Dependencies

None. No new packages; the parser is hand-written (a regex cannot express balanced-brace nesting
with escapes, and a dependency here would be a supply-chain surface on the security-critical path).

## 6. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Marker grammar and segment parser

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/sanitizer/user-input-markers.ts`.
  - Export `InputSegment`, `MARKER_TAGS` (closed `Set`), and
    `parseUserInputMarkers(text: string): readonly InputSegment[]`.
  - Export `class UserInputMarkerError extends Error` carrying `{ offset: number; reason: 'unterminated' | 'unknown_tag' | 'empty_value' | 'value_too_long' | 'reserved_placeholder' }`
    and a message naming the 1-based column.
  - Scanner: on `@@` emit a literal `@` and advance 2. On `@` + optional `[a-z_]+` + `{`, begin a
    marker; an intervening tag not in `MARKER_TAGS` (or equal to `auth_param`) throws
    `unknown_tag`. A bare `@` not followed by a valid marker opening is literal (so `a@b.com`
    parses untouched).
  - Body scan with `depth = 1`: `\` + one of `{ } \` emits that character and advances 2; `\` +
    anything else emits a literal `\` and advances 1; `{` increments depth; `}` decrements and
    closes at 0. EOF with `depth > 0` throws `unterminated`.
  - Nested markers are **not** re-parsed: `@{a @{b} c}` yields the literal value `a @{b} c`.
  - Reject a trim-empty value (`empty_value`) and a value over 2048 chars (`value_too_long`).
  - Reject input where `containsUserInputPlaceholder(text)` is true (`reserved_placeholder`).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `user-input-markers.spec.ts`, tagged `@no-llm`.
  - Bare `@{p1}` → one value segment, tag `secret`; `@password{p1}` → tag `password`.
  - Balanced braces: `@{{"k":"v"}}` → `{"k":"v"}`; `@{a{b}c}` → `a{b}c`.
  - Escapes: `@{p\}1}` → `p}1`; `@{a\\b}` → `a\b`; `@{C:\Users\x}` → `C:\Users\x` unchanged.
  - `@@{x}` → literal text `@{x}`, zero value segments.
  - `a@b.com` and `user@example.org` → single literal segment (no `@` false positive).
  - Errors, each asserting `reason` and column: `@{unterminated`, `@passwrd{x}`, `@auth_param{x}`,
    `@{}`, `@{   }`, 2049-char value, `do the {{user:email:1}} thing`.
  - `@{C:\Users\x\}` throws `unterminated` (documented consequence of `\}`).
  - Property test: for any generated segment list, `parse(render(segments))` round-trips, where
    `render` re-emits markers with minimal escaping.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on every export, including a grammar block and the rationale

- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test user-input-markers` passes; every error case

### TASK-003: Placeholder-aware, length-tiered echo masking

- [ ] **Implementation**: Rework `UserInputVault.mask()`.
  - Pre-scan the text for `PLACEHOLDER_RE` spans and never replace inside them. This is a real bug
    today, not a hypothetical: `{{user:secret:1}}` contains the substring `user`, which
    `isStandalonePosition` reports as standalone (delimited by `{` and `:`), so masking a value of
    `user` would rewrite the inside of a placeholder.
  - Tier by value length: `>= 8` keeps substring masking; `< 8` masks only at occurrences where
    `isStandalonePosition(text, offset, length)` holds.
  - Keep longest-first ordering; build output left-to-right so offsets stay valid, and treat each
    inserted placeholder as protected against subsequent values.
  - Add `warnOnShortValues(): readonly string[]` (or fold into the TASK-006 warning channel)
    reporting values under 3 characters, whose echo-masking is boundary-only and may miss.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: extend `user-input.spec.ts`, tagged `@no-llm`.
  - Value `u1`: masks standalone `u1` in `logged in as u1`; leaves `Ju1ce` and `u12` untouched.
  - Value `user`: `mask('{{user:secret:1}}')` returns the placeholder **unchanged**.
  - A 16-digit card still masks as a substring inside `id=4111111111111111&x=1`.
  - Overlapping values (`abc` and `abcdef`) mask longest-first with no partial clobber.
  - `mask()` is idempotent: `mask(mask(t)) === mask(t)`.
  - Property test: `mask()` never produces a string containing a stored raw value.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `mask()` explaining why the masking threshold differs from
      the redaction threshold, and that masking is defense-in-depth for echoed values while redaction

- **Verify**: a run marking `@{u1}` produces tool output where standalone `u1` is tokenized and no

### TASK-004: Keyword look-around detection

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/sanitizer/user-input-keywords.ts` exporting a
      segment transform `detectKeywordValues(segments, assign): readonly InputSegment[]`.
  - Keyword → tag map: `username|user ?id|userid|login|account name` → `username`;
    `password|passwd|pwd|passcode|pass` → `password`; `pin` → `pin`;
    `otp|one[- ]time (code|password)|2fa|mfa` → `otp`; `cvv|cvc` → `credit_card`;
    `ssn|social( security)?|national id|tax id` → `national_id`; `vin` → `vin`;
    `account (number|no|#)` → `account`.
  - Grammar: `<keyword> <connector>{0,2} <separator>? <value>`, connectors from a closed set
    (`is|are|of|my|the|for|as`), separators `: = -`, value = a quoted run (`"..."`, `'...'`) or a
    whitespace-delimited token terminated by whitespace, `,`, `;`, or a sentence-final `.`.
  - **Firing gate** — fire when _any_ holds:
    1. an explicit separator (`:`, `=`, `is`) is present; or
    2. the candidate has value-shape — contains a digit, or a non-alphanumeric character, or is
       not pure lowercase alpha; or
    3. the keyword is high-risk (`password`, `passwd`, `pwd`, `passcode`, `pin`, `cvv`, `cvc`,
       `otp`) **and** the candidate is not in the following-noun stoplist (`manager`, `managers`,
       `reset`, `field`, `box`, `prompt`, `strength`, `policy`, `protected`).
  - Never consume a candidate that is itself the next keyword (`username u1, password p1` must
    yield two values, not one).
  - Register the pass in `redact()` **before** the shape detectors (TASK-002 ordering).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `user-input-keywords.spec.ts`, tagged `@no-llm`.
  - The motivating case: `enter website xyz with username u1, password p1` → `u1` tagged
    `username`, `p1` tagged `password`, `xyz` untouched.
  - Separator forms: `password: hunter2`, `password=hunter2`, `password is hunter2`,
    `my password is "hunter 2"` (quoted, space preserved).
  - **Must not fire**: `search for password managers`, `reset my password`, `the password field`,
    `how strong is password strength scoring`.
  - `ssn 123-45-6789` tags `national_id` and the value never reaches the `ssn` shape pass.
  - `password 4111111111111111` tags `password`, not `credit_card` (ordering proof).
  - Case-insensitive, and tolerant of two connectors (`password for my account is x`).
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Module header stating explicitly that this layer is English-anchored
      and best-effort, that it exists for users who did not mark anything, and that `@{...}` is the
      region-agnostic guarantee.
- **Verify**: the four "must not fire" phrases produce zero placeholders; the motivating sentence

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: No change to secret resolution. Marked values are _user-supplied plaintext for this
  run_, deliberately distinct from keychain-backed opaque secret references, which remain the right
  mechanism for durable credentials. The doc must say so, so markers are not adopted as a
  credential store. Both share the posture that values materialize only at the execution boundary.
- **Error Handling**: `UserInputMarkerError` is a typed `Error` subclass per memory's custom-error
  rule, carrying `offset` and `reason`. It is thrown at ingress before any run state exists, so it
  is a validation error (exit 1), not an execution failure (exit 2) — no task failure event or
  report is emitted because no run was created. Error messages carry the column and reason but
  **never the offending value**.
- **Logging**: Per memory, never log raw sensitive payloads. Logs record marker _counts by tag_
  (`{ markers: { password: 1, username: 1 } }`) and never values, offsets into values, or lengths
  precise enough to narrow a short secret. The existing vault rule stands unchanged: raw values
  live in memory for one run and are never serialized into artifacts or prompts.
- **Performance**: The parser is a single O(n) scan; detector passes run over shrinking literal
  spans, so the segment model is never slower than today's chained `replace()`. The 2048-char value
  cap and the existing goal byte cap bound the work.
